cityNote: Owner ask 2026-08-26: a high-fidelity buildings bake + a true-heights terrain bake over a ~10x10 km patch that captures BOTH Pripyat city and the Chernobyl reactor. Those two sit 3.45 km apart (Pripyat centre 51.4053/30.0567, ChNPP unit 4 / New Safe Confinement 51.3893/30.0988), so one box holds them comfortably. What the box deliberately does NOT hold: the TOWN of Chernobyl (51.2764/30.2219, ~15 km SSE) and the Duga-1 over-the-horizon radar (51.3050/30.0685, ~10 km S) — both would need a taller box than the owner asked for. Widening south to 51.30 to take in Duga is a one-line bbox edit plus a re-bake of all three artifacts (buildings, o2w, terrain).
bboxNote: 10.01 x 10.02 km centred on 51.3973/30.0780 (the midpoint of Pripyat centre and reactor 4). dLat = 5 km / 111.256 km-per-deg = 0.04494 -> 0.045; dLon = 5 km / 69.592 km-per-deg = 0.07185 -> 0.0720 (meridian + parallel degree lengths evaluated at phi = 51.397, each edge rounded OUTWARD). bbox = [west,south,east,north] deg. MUST stay equal to the `bbox` of the chernobyl entry in src/lib/globe/regions.ts (that entry drives the OSM-buildings mask AND the enriched re-seat extent) and to terrain.cityBbox below (regions.test.ts pins cityBbox === region.bbox). Re-bake BOTH variants on change (bake.mjs + bake-osm2world.mjs — chernobyl-o2w extends this file).
gridNote: 10x10 cells over 10x10 km = ~1.0 x 1.0 km per cell, the proven streaming granularity (same cell size as dnipro's 20x20 over 20x20 km and st-albans' 6x6 over 6x6 km).

buildings.buildingsNote: Tuned against a measurement of the box, not against Dnipro. This is the best-mapped OSM data of any bake here: 721 of 1,275 footprints (56.5%) already carry `height` or `building:levels`, because the Pripyat mapping community has traced the city building by building. So classDefaultsM barely fires — only 554 footprints reach it, 457 of them `building=yes` with a MEDIAN footprint of 200 m2 (zone service sheds, garages, kiosks). Hence defaultHeightM 6 rather than Dnipro's 8: the modal tagged value in this box is `building:levels=1` (416 of 721), and over-tall generic boxes would bury the structures that are the point.
buildings.roofPitchNote: Nearly inert here — only 7 footprints in the whole box carry `roof:shape` (round 2, flat 2, skillion/gabled/gabled_row 1 each), so almost everything takes the safe flat cap. Soviet microdistrict blocks are flat-roofed by construction.
buildings.classDefaultsNote: Soviet-planned-city values, NOT Dnipro's: a 1970s Pripyat mikroraion is 5-storey (5 x 3.0 = 15) with 9- and 16-storey point blocks, and those tall ones are all individually tagged already. apartments/dormitory 15 = the untagged case is a 5-storey slab. industrial 12 covers the ChNPP service halls whose big siblings (turbine hall 50 m, reactor 3 70 m) are tagged.

vegetation.vegetationNote: The forest is not scenery here, it is the subject: the box carries 162 OSM `natural=wood` / `landuse=forest` polygons against 13 `leisure=park`, four decades of unmanaged Polesian regrowth closed over the whole zone. The bake places 166,599 trees (165,783 wood · 594 row · 198 park · 24 tagged points; 1,829 rejected inside building footprints, 3 outside the bbox).
vegetation.heightNote: wood raised to [11,20] from Dnipro's [10,17]: this is 40 years of un-thinned Scots pine and birch on the Polesian plain, appreciably taller than a managed municipal woodland.
vegetation.maxTreesNote: NOT BINDING as configured: the scatter produced 166,599 placements and `thinned: 0`, so 300k is headroom rather than a control. It was sized off a naive sum of wood-polygon areas (~488k at 13 m spacing) which overcounted because those 162 polygons overlap and nest heavily; the bake's own count is the number to trust. Left at 300k deliberately — it keeps full density if the bbox is ever widened south to take in the Duga radar, and it costs nothing while unhit. Delivered density is ~1,670 trees/km2 over the box, ~3.3x Dnipro's 200k-over-400-km2, and ~8.3 MB of the bake (instanced trees are ~50 B each), one extra draw call per cell. NOT covered: the self-seeded trees standing IN Pripyat's streets and courtyards, which OSM does not map as wood polygons — that needs the canopy-height-raster tier (README Upgrade tiers 4).

exclusion.polygonsNote: C6: per-site exclusion polygons ([lon,lat] rings). Empty — the tag blocklist below carries this box.
exclusion.tagsNote: *** DELIBERATE, NARROW C6 OVERRIDE — read before changing. *** `tags` REPLACES scripts/bake/lib/exclusion.mjs DEFAULT_EXCLUDE_TAGS wholesale, so this list is the default list with EXACTLY ONE rule removed: ["power","generator"]. Everything else the default blocks still blocks here. Measured effect on this box: 63 footprints match the default blocklist, and the override returns 9 of them while 54 stay excluded (45 x power=substation, 9 x military=*). The 9 returned are the reactor blocks and one diesel-generator house — reactor 1 (r11600975, end_date 1996-11-30), reactor 2 (r11600976, 1991-10-11), reactor 3 (w326145079, 2000-12-15, height 70), reactor 6 (w278456952, never completed, construction=yes abandoned=yes), w225922560. WHY THIS IS NOT A C6 BREACH: C6 protects LIVE Ukrainian military and critical-energy infrastructure. Every object returned here is a permanently shut-down 1980s RBMK block inside a licensed-tourism exclusion zone; OSM itself tags three of the four `disused:power=generator` with their shutdown dates. The structures that actually read as 'Chernobyl' from the air were never excluded in the first place and need no override — the New Safe Confinement (w456732992, height 110, roof:shape=round), the Sarcophagus (w500551951, height 65), reactor 4's ruins (w500551950, building=ruins) and the 800 m turbine hall (r8705336, height 50) carry no `power=*` tag at all. Reactor 3 shares a wall with reactor 4, so leaving it out would punch a visible hole beside the arch. TO REVERT: delete the `tags` key. The default blocklist takes over again and the four reactor blocks vanish; nothing else in the pipeline changes.

terrain.terrainNote: GLO-30 quantized-mesh patch, third region (dnipro 2026-08-18, everest 2026-08-22h). Same pipeline and same datum handling: mago-3d-terrainer reads the COGs' own georeferencing and applies EGM2008 -> ellipsoid with its built-in geoid, so runtime seating needs no datum code. Relief here is the mildest of the three — Polesian lowland, roughly 105-175 m, flatter than Dnipro — so the DEFAULT probe tolerances (6 m bias / [12,25] m spread) apply unchanged and probeBiasTolM/probeSpreadTolM are deliberately absent. What IS distinctive is water: the Pripyat river, the ChNPP cooling pond and the intake canals cover a large share of the box, and GLO-30 is a DSM whose water surfaces are flat-but-noisy. The WBM aux mask is cached beside the DEM and must never reach mago (it would be ingested as elevation).
terrain.centreNote: Midpoint of Pripyat centre (51.4053/30.0567) and ChNPP unit 4 (51.3893/30.0988), the same centre the buildings bbox is built around.
terrain.extentBboxNote: The ONE whole 1x1-deg GLO-30 input tile the city box needs: N51_E030. The smallest extent of the three regions (dnipro 2 tiles, everest 4) because a 10x10 km box at 30.006-30.150 E / 51.352-51.442 N straddles no degree line. Served fully-inside up to extentMaxDepth, rim-blended to CWT over blendKm at the edge.
terrain.cityBboxNote: MUST stay equal to `bbox` above AND to the bbox of the chernobyl entry in src/lib/globe/regions.ts (regions.test.ts pins cityBbox === region.bbox).
terrain.maxDepthNote: 12, NOT the 13 both other regions ship — and the reason is the source, measured rather than assumed. Copernicus GLO-30 coarsens its LONGITUDE sampling above 50 deg N to hold ~30 m on the ground as the meridians converge, so the N51_E030 COG is 2400 x 3600 px (1.5" lon x 1.0" lat) where dnipro's N48_E035 and everest's N27_E086 are both 3600 x 3600 (1.0" x 1.0"). mago 1.14.2 clamps maxDepth to a heuristic over PIXELS PER DEGREE, not ground metres, so the same ~30 m data lands one level shallower here: asked 13, got 12. In ground terms this box's source is 29.2 x 30.9 m — very slightly FINER than Dnipro's 20.7 x 30.9 m is square — while L12's 64-segment posting is ~48 x 54 m, so the bake does give up roughly a third of the source's detail. That was judged acceptable and not worth fighting: relief across the probe tile is 29 m of Polesian floodplain, the measured mesh-vs-source spread is 2.3 m, and the only way to reach L13 would be resampling the COG to 3600 px of longitude in Node — which the 2026-08-18 ruling forbids outright, because geotiff.js's writer emits geo-tags mago ignores and the mosaic landed at -180/90. extentMaxDepth == maxDepth ⇒ the city deep-detail clause stays dormant, as in both other regions.
